newsitem.title: UK: Euro Products Outlook - Gas oil down, mogas up.
newsitem.headline: Euro Products Outlook - Gas oil down, mogas up.

text.p: European oil products face mixed prospects this week with gas oil possibly easing, gasoline looking firm and fuel and naphtha steady.
Gas oil prices were seen softening due to a dearth of buying interest,though the market remains underpinned by tighter supplies, traders said.

However, while more balanced in the north with a strong dollar seen continuing to dampen demand from the key German market, demand from the East Med should continue to see prices edging higher in the south.
Relaxed buying and good supply from Ventspils was also seen pressuring premiums for 0.2 sulphur.
Despite some light buying into Germany last week a small backwardation between prompt and early August deliveries was wiped out and the market could tip further into contango.
In contrast diesel remained well supported with recent busy trade taking out most of the surplus.

But the market to the end of August looked fairly flat with premiums to the August screen contained in a +$4/+$5 range for deliveries by August 15 and Aug 16-31 deliveries around Sep IPE +$4.50/+$5 a tonne.

Some traders expected high sulphur fuel oil barges to continue drawing strength from demand, with a few saying they could reach as high as $93. Others however saw the picture more or less stable at about $88/$90.
"We've been trading in a range of $80 to $90 for a month now and it is hard to say if they (barges) will break through that," one said.
High sulphur cargoes looked set to continue in the mid-80s cif with some more demand seen coming in.
"I certainly don't see it falling below the levels it has reached recently," a trader said.
Low sulphur cargoes should continue steady to a little stronger, with demand seen from traders willing to take material transatlantic with the arb said to be open.
Dealers saw naphtha strong relative to crude and other products, driven by an open arb from the Med to Asia and the U.S. Gulf and a healthy level of trader buying interest in NWE.
NWE was likely to remain around the current $190 value for prompt physical and August swaps, if not slightly higher.
A reluctance by European petchem end-users to come into the market at current levels was seen, although with propane remaining above naphtha feedstock options were limited.
Gasoline was seen to have good prospects if U.S. prices consolidated or improved on last week's rally and naphtha continued well-bid.
Refiners may be tempted to maximise output of naphtha at the expense of gasoline and thus heighten what some see as an already tight market in the north.
Arbitrage to the U.S. will be an option for some traders and will act as support keeping eurograde cargoes around $190 cif NWE.
